_doc: GATE EVIDENCE DOCKET (machine-readable; human view GATE_EVIDENCE_DOCKET.md). Owner order 2026-08-31: keep a manifest of everything the adversary gate and its enforcement layers CATCH and force into remediation - the running evidentiary case for the mandatory adversarial commit gate and the layered structure (and for the harness-native version proposed in anthropics/claude-code#90887).
_covenant: Every catch that forces a remediation gets a row IN THE SAME WORKING SESSION as the catch: date, repo, layer (gate-review BLOCK / pre-commit wall / post-commit notary / push guard / auditor / harness guard / CI / advisor second-reviewer), what was caught, severity, whether the author initially disputed it (false rebuttals are the strongest rows - they prove authors defend invented claims, the gate's founding thesis), the resolution, and artifact references. Rows are never deleted; a catch later shown false is amended in place with the evidence.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (six adversarial rounds on the gate's own birth code)
entries.caught: Merge-commit bypass (merges exempted from review); empty-model-response IndexError crash; hook-edit bypass (extension filter waved .githooks edits through); code-deletion/rename-away bypass; a literal BEL byte the author had dismissed as a rendering artifact; a per-clone-arming overpromise in the shim's own banner.
entries.severity: HIGH (multiple independent bypass classes in the enforcement tool itself)
entries.author_initially: Defended several; round 5 caught FALSE REBUTTAL #1 - the author claimed fixes that a failed edit driver had never written; the adversary read the staged bytes and proved the claim false.
entries.resolution: All six classes fixed and re-reviewed to CLEAR before the gate's first arming; the empty-response fail-closed BLOCK later proved itself live (EV-004).

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (seven rounds on install_gate.py)
entries.caught: Eleven real findings including CRLF-corrupted-shim blessing, foreign-hooksPath equivalence misjudgment, and fail-closed-vs-armed exit-contract gaps.
entries.severity: HIGH
entries.author_initially: Round 6 caught FALSE REBUTTAL #2 - the author claimed the chmod=+x step was already in the NEXT-steps text; it was not.
entries.resolution: All fixed; installer selftest grew to cover every claim (38/38 today).

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (review of Caliper's own arming commit)
entries.caught: The staged hook was index mode 100644 - POSIX git SILENTLY SKIPS a non-executable hook, so the mandatory gate was fully DISARMED on any POSIX checkout. All three previously-armed repos had shipped the same fail-open.
entries.severity: CRITICAL (the whole gate a no-op on POSIX clones)
entries.author_initially: Accepted immediately.
entries.resolution: update-index --chmod=+x + .gitattributes LF pins everywhere; installer NEXT text and selftests now enforce it; G35 row GATE-HOOK-MODE-100644.

entries.layer: gate-review runtime behavior (fail-closed proof, not an author error)
entries.caught: The default reviewer hung ~50 minutes and returned NO content; the gate printed '(model returned no content - failing closed)' and BLOCKed instead of crashing or silently clearing - the exact behavior EV-001's empty-response fix was built for.
entries.severity: evidence-of-design (a permissive gate would have shipped an unreviewed commit)
entries.author_initially: n/a
entries.resolution: Review re-run on z-ai/glm-5.2 (now the recommended flag); the same failure mode later got an auto-retry guard in hy4-review (EV-010).

entries.layer: advisor second-reviewer (design review before the layered build)
entries.caught: The trivial bypass of the entire hook architecture: an agent writing .adversary/clearance.json directly with correct staged sha256s - a forged clearance notarizes cleanly and audits green; layers 1/3/4 cannot see it. Identified BEFORE the build; became the pivot of the layer-2 design.
entries.severity: CRITICAL (silent total bypass)
entries.author_initially: Had not considered it.
entries.resolution: harness_guard.py denies every .adversary/** write path (file tools AND Bash) plus notes mutation and update-ref; registered machine-wide by the owner.

entries.repo: Tools (caught live on Nexusmill's first guarded push)
entries.layer: pre-push guard (the layer caught its own defect in production)
entries.caught: rev-list's --not flag TOGGLES: the guard's '--not <remote> --not <baseline>' range re-INCLUDED the entire pre-baseline history and refused a fully notarized push. The selftest had only covered the remote-sha-zero shape, where a single --not is emitted.
entries.severity: MEDIUM (false refusal; fail-safe direction, but would have blocked every real push)
entries.author_initially: n/a (self-caught by the layer's refusal output on first live use)
entries.resolution: Single --not with all exclusions; regression test push_guard_remote_plus_baseline; G35 row GATE-PUSH-DOUBLE-NOT; playbook troubleshooting entry.

entries.layer: advisor second-reviewer (CI design)
entries.caught: The audit workflow's pull_request trigger checks out GitHub's server-side synthetic merge commit, which can never carry a note - every PR would have been flagged a VIOLATION forever, and with enforce_admins protection, merges would have locked permanently.
entries.severity: HIGH (layer 4 would have been unusable)
entries.author_initially: Shipped the trigger before the catch.
entries.resolution: Workflows are push-only with the rationale in-file; playbook chapter 4 + troubleshooting entry.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (fresh eyes on byte-copies of ALREADY-CLEARED code)
entries.caught: Three real portability defects in code every line of which had passed review in its home repo: (HIGH) adversary_gate.py's hardcoded git path with no PATH fallback - the distributed gate dead on arrival on any non-authoring machine; (MED) the refusal message instructing users to run a path that exists only on the authoring machine; (LOW) two selftests with the same hardcoded git path.
entries.severity: HIGH (the public offering would not have functioned anywhere else)
entries.author_initially: Framed the bundle as 'byte-copies of cleared canonicals' expecting a rubber stamp.
entries.resolution: All three fixed in the Tools canonicals (d7d496f), re-bundled, re-reviewed to CLEAR. Context matters: 'already reviewed' is a property of a diff in a repo, not of bytes.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK, two rounds, plus live platform counter-evidence
entries.caught: Round 1: the author's rebase-only merge fallback was BACKWARDS security logic - under linear-history protection the rebase button WORKS and mints N unaudited shas onto the protected branch, while the merge button is inert; the status line also claimed 'merge buttons off' while enabling one. Round 2: after the platform refused the reviewer's ideal too (422 protected_branch_policy), the reviewer caught the module docstring still promising 'buttons are DISABLED' and an unconditional fast-forward-only guarantee that squash-only had broken.
entries.severity: HIGH (unaudited shas reachable on protected branches + overstated security posture)
entries.author_initially: Argued 'least-harmful residue' with reversed reasoning; conceded on re-read.
entries.resolution: Squash-only floor (one unaudited sha per misuse instead of N; any use turns the audit red), truthful docstring and status lines, both live 422 constraints documented in code and playbook.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK
entries.caught: Two real defects in a 30-line guard: the empty-response retry unconditionally re-added a reasoning key the provider had already 400-rejected (crash loop with a raw traceback and no spend report), and the retry call lacked the HTTPError handling every other API call in the function has.
entries.severity: MEDIUM
entries.author_initially: FALSE REBUTTAL #3 - the author's context claimed 'the retry only runs when reasoning was accepted'; the guard had no such check. The reviewer quoted the actual condition.
entries.resolution: reasoning_ok flag gating the guard; wrapped retry with the wasted first-call usage in the error; conceded in the re-review context.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK
entries.caught: A helper-import side effect had doubled the status/resolution KEY PAIR inside one deferred-manifest object - json.loads silently keeps the last duplicate, so the author's own 'manifest validates' claim was true-but-meaningless; the reviewer distinguished duplicate array ids (checked) from duplicate object keys (not checked).
entries.severity: LOW (identical values; but malformed under strict validation, and a validator blind spot)
entries.author_initially: Claimed validation had passed - it had, for the wrong property.
entries.resolution: Pair removed; a strict object_pairs_hook duplicate-key sweep adopted as the standing validation for every governance-JSON edit since.

entries.layer: harness guard (layer 2, live)
entries.caught: Within the hour of registration the guard blocked its OWN AUTHOR twice: a commit message containing the word 'hooksPath' in prose, and a plain ls of .adversary/reviews. Both were the documented accepted-false-positive class; both times the author reworded or used gate tooling rather than weakening the guard.
entries.severity: evidence-of-design (enforcement holding against the agent that built it)
entries.author_initially: n/a
entries.resolution: No change - working as designed; the precedent 'reword, never weaken' is now in the playbook.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (on a data-sync commit the author expected to pass trivially)
entries.caught: Real mixed-era schema drift in the review-archive manifest: 13 rows without the rel/modes wrapper, three output-path conventions, ten source files dual-keyed with their review record fragmented across incompatible entries - a generator defect nobody had noticed across weeks of syncs.
entries.severity: MEDIUM (consumer contract split)
entries.author_initially: Rebutted the FIX location (hand-editing generator data would falsify the record and desync the writer) - the rebuttal was verified and accepted; the DEFECT was conceded and docketed.
entries.resolution: Docketed OPEN as deferred COLIBRI-ARCHIVE-SCHEMA; the archive committed as ground truth. EXECUTED same day under the audit campaign (amendment per covenant): the real writer proved to be review SESSIONS hand-editing the manifest against an ambiguous skill instruction - normalize_manifest() shipped in repo-memory (read-side tolerance + archive-write normalization, TDD), one-shot normalization of both corpora recovered ALL FIFTEEN review records that had been invisible to every consumer (visible modes 102->117, dual keys folded 99->88 entries), and the skill instruction was sharpened to the exact canonical shape in all three copies including the public plugin. The first normalizer version destroyed two colliding records - caught by the gate, EV-016 - before the corrected collision-safe version produced these numbers.

entries.layer: auditor-mindset sweep during remediation (found because the gate forces manifest reads)
entries.caught: A structural filing disease across BOTH governance manifests: three G35 remediation rows appended into a nested findings[] array instead of entries[], and ALL EIGHT HY4 spec dockets appended into entries_archived (the closed pile) - every consumer iterating the live arrays missed them. Cause: tail-anchored surgical inserts following whatever object closes last.
entries.severity: MEDIUM (open work invisible to the queues that exist to track it)
entries.author_initially: The author's own earlier sessions had created the misfilings.
entries.resolution: Owner-ruled restructures: rows moved verbatim into the live arrays; the anchor trap recorded in the governance-editing memory; strict validation now walks the actual tree.
refs: Nexusmill e471915 + the HY4 move in c9ac5d0

entries.repo: Nexusmill (harness over PatternSkin + Asset Forge + caseview)
entries.layer: features critic (the harness's own DRIFT/FAIL/undeclared ratchet - a detection layer in the same family as the auditor)
entries.caught: Roughly two dozen covenant violations by PAST sessions, invisible until the post-gate audit ran the tier: five tester FAILs that were all STALENESS masking evolved-STRONGER code (the sam3 zero-decode protection, the broadened generator guard, the ruled refuse-not-substitute transparency contract); four registry anchors orphaned by refactors; one battery still asserting an owner-OVERRULED design (the dishonest white-backdrop downgrade) as if it were the contract; THIRTEEN green batteries that existed but were never wired to their rows (their features counted as tested by nobody); and nine rows with genuinely no coverage, shipped without testers by the sessions that added them.
entries.severity: HIGH in aggregate (the harness's verdicts had quietly stopped meaning anything for a fifth of the registry)
entries.author_initially: Past sessions - this agent included - repeatedly shipped feature rows and refactors without the same-commit tester/registry updates the covenant demands; nothing enforced it until the audit.
entries.resolution: Tranche 3976f63: staleness fixed WITH git -S evidence per item (never blind re-fixed - G35), the overruled battery reworked to the ruled contract, thirteen batteries wired (system-python isolation for Blender-lacking deps), nine debts DECLARED in the ratchet allowlist with reasons. Features tier green for the first time in weeks: 0 FAIL, 0 DRIFT, 0 undeclared. The row itself argues for gating registry edits the way code is gated - which the .json-as-code ruling already began.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (on the normalized-archive commit - a REMEDIATION reviewed like any change)
entries.caught: The remediation for EV-013 itself destroyed data: the first normalize_manifest resolved a mode-name collision with 'canonical wins', silently discarding the wrapperless side - and the reviewer traced the actual diff to prove the two colliding library_gen.py records were DIFFERENT legitimate reviews (distinct shas, dates 08-12/08-13, one carrying a substantive cross-file audit note). It also caught the arithmetic cover: '13 recovered' was true only because 15 existed and 2 were silently dropped.
entries.severity: MEDIUM (permanent loss of two paid review records, inside a fix whose stated rule was 'never destroys')
entries.author_initially: Claimed 'canonical data preserved on every collision' - accurate about the canonical side, silent about the discarded side; the reviewer read the deletion out of the staged diff.
entries.resolution: Collision-safe rework, RED-first: identical sha = dedupe; different sha = newer reviewed_at holds the bare key, the other preserved under the sanctioned synthetic key mode@sha8. Corpora restored from the archive's committed HEAD (the BLOCK had stopped the bad version from landing) and re-normalized: all FIFTEEN records preserved, visible modes 102->117, verified per-entry. The meta-lesson joins the docket: remediations destroy data too - review them like any change.

entries.layer: gate-review advisory note inside a CLEAR (tranche-8 commit 87cb8f29)
entries.caught: The tranche-8 registry truth-pass corrected the colour-hint library count (70->69; GREY-MUSH-1/487781a0 deliberately removed one hint) in AF-LIB-HINTS' expected text and verify field - but MISSED the second stale '70 hints' sitting in AF-STUDIO-HINTS' expected text three rows away. The GLM reviewer flagged the leftover in its clearance notes while granting CLEAR.
entries.severity: LOW (stale registry documentation; no code effect - but a truth-pass that fixes one occurrence of a wrong number and declares victory is the exact half-measure the docket exists to record)
entries.author_initially: Declared the 70->69 correction complete after editing only the row the failing battery check pointed at; never grepped the registry for other occurrences of the stale count.
entries.resolution: Same session, pre-commit: the second occurrence corrected with the same git citation, features tier re-run green, commit re-gated (the re-edit invalidated the prior clearance exactly as designed) and landed in Nexusmill 87cb8f29. Lesson: a truth-pass on a number greps for EVERY occurrence of the old number before claiming completeness.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK x3 - two findings BLOCKs (r1, r3) + one fail-closed empty-content BLOCK (r2) - on the commit that promoted deepseek-v4-flash-0731 to primary (its first official reviews)
entries.caught: The model-fallback-chain change (owner ruling: deepseek primary, glm-5.3-flash fallback) drew three BLOCK verdicts before its CLEAR - findings BLOCKs in r1 and r3 from the new primary reviewing its own promotion, and r2's fail-closed BLOCK on an empty response. r1: --model '' / ADVERSARY_MODEL='' produce an empty chain and `raise None` (TypeError) behind the author's comment 'unreachable (empty chain is impossible: argparse default is non-empty)' - a false claim about reachability. r3: URLError (connection refused/DNS/TLS/timeout - the canonical transport failure the chain was BUILT for) never converts to SystemExit, so the chain crashed with a raw traceback instead of falling back; and the DEFAULT_MODEL comment still documented the pre-amendment empty-response behavior, contradicting the code about the EV-004 invariant. Between them, r2's blind fail-closed BLOCK on deepseek's empty-content response (32,677 reasoning tokens, zero answer text) exposed the operational hazard that reshaped the design to chain-advance-on-empty.
entries.severity: MEDIUM (a crash path, a dead fallback, and an unhandled empty-response operational hazard in the safety tool itself - the last reshaping the design to chain-advance-on-empty - plus two wrong claims in its security comments, all in the change that was supposed to make the gate MORE reliable)
entries.author_initially: Declared the empty chain 'impossible' in a comment (wrong: two reachable inputs produce it) and left a security comment asserting an invariant the amended code no longer implemented.
entries.resolution: All fixed pre-commit: empty chain fails closed with a clean error; URLError converts to SystemExit so the chain advances; the comment now states the SURVIVING invariant (empty can never CLEAR; a last-model empty still BLOCKs). The final CLEAR arrived through the new fallback path exercising itself live - deepseek returned empty content on the gate's own file twice and glm-5.3-flash completed the review. Landed as Tools dca6ae4; Tools pushed to github.com/Nexusmill/Tools (private) after a full-history secrets scan (209 objects, zero hits).
refs: gate_20260901-102316.md (Tools reviews - r2 empty-content fail-closed BLOCK)
gate_20260901-104924.md (Tools reviews - CLEAR via the fallback)

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (campaign tranche 15, first review)
entries.caught: The new PS-LIB battery's row-grading split let every run-integrity failure fail only ONE of its two rows: with no Blender on the machine, with the inner probe crashing before its first check, or - the primary regression class the battery exists to catch - with the PACKAGED add-on failing to enable (or silently loading the machine's installed copy instead of the sandbox), PS-LIB-FLAT-INSTALL graded PASS with ZERO of its checks executed; symmetrically a mid-run death after one LIBG_ line left PS-LIB-GENERATE green on unexecuted claims. The reviewer traced all four trigger paths from the staged bytes and named the fix shape.
entries.severity: HIGH (false-green coverage rows - the untested ratchet would have believed debt paid on evidence that never ran)
entries.author_initially: Had built the mid-run-death guard for exactly this class but scoped it to one row - in the reviewer's words, 'it just stops one row short'. Accepted immediately.
entries.resolution: Run-integrity guards renamed LIBRUN_ (no-Blender / inner-never-ran / inner-died-mid-run / loaded-from-wrong-place / ops-unregistered) and appended to BOTH rows' fail lists; each row additionally requires at least one of its OWN check lines to have executed (else it reads 'no ... checks executed', red). Verified by trace in the re-review: the no-Blender scenario reds both rows; features tier green end-to-end; CLEAR on r2.

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK (pre-commit, campaign phase-2 tranche-1 sweep reviews)
entries.caught: Two confident-wrong claims in the AGENT'S OWN gated colibri-review deliverables (not the code under review): (1) the guard_selftest.py review labeled GLM's cwd finding 'MEDIUM refuted' and SILENTLY DROPPED GLM's actual MEDIUM (run_guard has no subprocess timeout -> selftest can hang forever), asserting false provenance; (2) the adversary_audit.py review said 'ALL ten locations' then enumerated nine vendored twins, an off-by-one in the re-vendor checklist that would silently leave one copy on stale gate code.
entries.severity: LOW-MEDIUM (false-provenance + dropped-finding in the review archive; the gate treats a wrong claim in a deliverable as the same defect class it exists to prevent)
entries.author_initially: Wrote both claims as fact. The gate (glm-5.3-flash primary) BLOCKed and named both; the author ADDRESSED (did not rebut) - confirmed the real timeout MEDIUM, relabeled the cwd finding LOW-refuted, and reconciled the count to 1 canonical + 9 vendored = 10.
entries.resolution: Both review .md corrected; re-staged; gate re-run to CLEAR before the Tools commit. Lesson: an external review's severities and full finding set must be carried into the gated review verbatim - relabeling or dropping a finding is the same confident-wrong class the sweep is hunting.

entries.layer: gate run CRASH (L0 fail-closed surfaced a latent defect in the gate's OWN code during live use)
entries.caught: While gating the phase-2 remediation's Nexusmill manifest commit, adversary_gate._call_one_model crashed with JSONDecodeError: OpenRouter returned a 200 with an HTML proxy-error body, and json.loads sat inside a try whose except only handled HTTPError/URLError, so the error escaped _call_model's SystemExit-only chain handler and killed cmd_run instead of failing over to the fallback model. The gate could not run -> it blocked its own remediation commit.
entries.severity: MEDIUM (availability: a flaky provider bricks the gate instead of failing over; fail-closed so no false CLEAR)
entries.author_initially: This exact MEDIUM was DOCUMENTED in the phase-2 adversary_gate.py sweep review but not fixed (it was not in the owner's top-5). It then bit live. Fixed immediately (Tools 9b60573): non-JSON body -> SystemExit (chain advances), null choices coerced.
entries.resolution: Verified modelA-bad-body -> modelB failover + null-choices no-crash + gate_selftest 32/32; committed 9b60573; remediation row GATE-MALFORMED-200-CRASH. Lesson: a documented-but-deferred defect in the enforcement tool itself can block the very work that would fix everything - the gate's fail-closed crash is what surfaced it.
refs: gate run gate_20260902-135030 (the CLEAR after the fix)

entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK x8 + one byte-cited rebuttal (the phase-2 sweep's harness_guard residual fix, reviewed over eight rounds)
entries.caught: Closing two documented harness_guard residuals (compound-command exemption + shell-var commit-bypass smuggle) took EIGHT gate rounds; the gate found a REAL agent-reachable forgery route or integrity defect nearly every round: (r1) a write-indicator denylist missed python open()/git config --file/curl -o/node -e/find -delete writes; (r2) a first-word read-allowlist ignored a redirect/heredoc still in the segment; (r3) process substitution + xxd outfile operand + export-prefixed var assignments; (r4) shell-FUNCTION laundering (a reader-named function definition); (r5) cross-segment function laundering + PATH hijack (per-segment eval severed def from invoke; argv[0]=='cat' guarantees nothing runs cat); (r6-r8) shallow var-flag bypasses + author overclaims + a STAGING MISMATCH (the fix was on disk but a denied stage command left the round-6 bytes staged; the gate proved 'the tree you verified is not the tree being committed'). Final design: NO read exemption on the state dir - block any reference; reads go through the status subcommand - the only thing a text guard can do safely once shadowing/PATH/aliases exist.
entries.severity: HIGH (each round was a live forgery route into the state dir's clearance file - the one bypass with no backstop - or a verification-integrity defect)
entries.author_initially: Overclaimed completeness twice (rounds 5-6) and staged the wrong bytes once (rounds 7-8); each caught and corrected. Round 8 was a gate MISREAD of the staged regex, settled by a byte-cited factual rebuttal (staged==disk; the staged decide() blocks all cited forms; guard_selftest 84/84 not 79/84) - the gate re-verified against the bytes and CLEARed.
entries.resolution: Committed Tools a72b051 after CLEAR; guard_selftest 41->84 (a regression per closed bypass); reason+docstring honestly scope the var rule as best-effort/audit-backstopped. LESSON: a regex cannot safely classify shell as read-vs-write; the secure move is to block the whole state dir and lean on the audit tripwire for the unbounded tail - and ALWAYS re-verify the STAGED bytes match the fix, since a denied stage command silently leaves old bytes staged.

entries.layer: pre-commit gate BLOCK (committing the copilot-branch's outstanding tracked edits before moving the repo to main)
entries.caught: A ~22,000-line addition to a tracked memory/session_learnings archive carried LIVE plaintext network credentials pasted from a terminal transcript: the LAN gateway's root password (a paramiko one-liner that demonstrably authenticated), the Wi-Fi AP admin password verbatim, and printer SSH creds. The agent had staged the whole tracked diff (git add -u) and was one commit away from writing those secrets into permanent git history - exactly the G18 'never commit secrets' violation the gate exists to stop. (Secret VALUES are deliberately not recorded in this docket - only the class.) The same review also flagged a LOW dangling dataset-index reference to an unstaged artifact.
entries.severity: HIGH (root/admin credential exposure to any future push/clone/backup of the repo)
entries.author_initially: Accepted the finding immediately - unstaged the credential-bearing file plus all memory/ transcript files and the dangling-index files, committed only the gate-cleared safe subset, and surfaced the exposure to the owner with a rotate-and-scrub recommendation (rotating live network credentials is an owner action, not taken unilaterally).
entries.resolution: 3DPrinting ec6a7e1e commits the safe subset only; the credential file stays a local uncommitted edit. Owner flagged to rotate the gateway root + AP admin passwords and scrub the file. LESSON: `git add -u` on a repo one hasn't worked in recently can sweep pasted-transcript secrets into history; the gate's content review - not just extension/path filtering - is what caught it.
